name: LM Studio (local AI server)
what: Free AI that runs on your own computer. Your app talks to it like it talks to ChatGPT.
signupSteps: Install LM Studio and download an AI (see our Free AI page)
Click the Developer tab, then turn on "Start server"
Your app connects to http://localhost:1234/v1
note: Works with any app built for the OpenAI API. Only works while your computer is on.

name: Ollama (local AI server)
what: Free AI on your own computer, for people who are okay typing a command or two.
signupSteps: Install Ollama from ollama.com
Type `ollama run qwen3:8b` once to download an AI
Your app connects to http://localhost:11434/v1

name: OpenRouter
what: One key that unlocks hundreds of AI models, including some free ones.
freeTier: Some free models: about 50 requests a day (more after you add $10 of credit)
paidFrom: Pay per use, depends on the model
signupSteps: Sign up at openrouter.ai
Go to Keys and click Create Key
Set a monthly spending limit in Settings
note: Free models come and go, so pick a backup model too.

name: Google AI Studio (Gemini API)
what: Google's Gemini AI for your app, with a free plan to start.
freeTier: Free plan with daily limits (see your limits inside AI Studio)
paidFrom: Pay per use after you turn on billing
signupSteps: Sign in at aistudio.google.com with a Google account
Click "Get API key" and create one
note: On the free plan, Google may use what you send to improve its products.

name: Groq
what: Very fast AI and speech-to-text, with a free plan to start.
freeTier: Free plan with daily limits, no card needed
signupSteps: Sign up at console.groq.com
Click API Keys and create one

name: Claude API (Anthropic)
what: The Claude AI for your own app. You pay only for what you use.
paidFrom: Pay per use (cents for most small apps)
signupSteps: Sign up at console.anthropic.com
Add a small amount of credit and set a spending limit
Create an API key

name: OpenAI API
what: The ChatGPT AIs for your own app. You pay only for what you use.
signupSteps: Sign up at platform.openai.com
Add a small amount of credit and set a spending limit
Create an API key

name: Resend
what: Sends emails from your app, like sign-up codes, receipts and reminders.
signupSteps: Sign up at resend.com
Add your website domain and follow the steps to verify it
Create an API key

name: Brevo
what: Sends emails and newsletters, with a big free daily allowance.
signupSteps: Sign up at brevo.com
Verify your sender email or domain
Create an API key under SMTP & API

name: Amazon SES
what: Very cheap email sending for big lists. Harder to set up.
freeTier: Small free allowance for new accounts
signupSteps: Make an AWS account
Verify your domain in SES
Ask AWS to move you out of "sandbox" mode so you can email anyone

name: SQLite
what: A tiny database that lives in one file inside your app. Nothing to sign up for.
signupSteps: Nothing to sign up for: your AI helper adds it to the app
goodFor: Apps just for you or your family
note: Back up the database file to keep your data safe.

name: PocketBase
what: A free database plus logins and file uploads, all in one small app you run yourself.
paidFrom: Always free; you only pay for your server
signupSteps: Download PocketBase for your computer
Run it and open the admin page in your browser
Create your first account and tables

name: Supabase
what: A hosted database with logins, file storage and live updates.
freeTier: 500 MB database, 1 GB files, 50,000 users a month; pauses after a week with no use
signupSteps: Sign up at supabase.com
Click New project and pick a password
Copy the project URL and anon key from Project Settings → API

name: Firebase (Google)
what: Google's hosted database and logins for apps.
signupSteps: Sign in at firebase.google.com with a Google account
Create a project and add a web app
Copy the config settings it shows you

name: Cloudflare Pages
what: Puts your website online for free, with no limit on visitors.
freeTier: Unlimited visitors for simple sites, 500 updates a month; business use allowed
signupSteps: Sign up at cloudflare.com
Go to Workers & Pages → Create → connect your GitHub
Pick your project and click Deploy

name: Vercel
what: Puts your website online with a few clicks. Great for Next.js apps.
freeTier: Free "Hobby" plan for personal projects only
paidFrom: Pro from $20 a month (needed for business use)
signupSteps: Sign up at vercel.com with GitHub
Click Add New → Project and pick your project
Click Deploy
note: The free plan is for personal, non-business use.

name: Netlify
what: Puts your website online. Business use is okay on the free plan.
signupSteps: Sign up at netlify.com with GitHub
Click Add new site → Import an existing project
Pick your project and click Deploy

name: Coolify
what: Your own free "Vercel" on a server you rent. Runs many apps in one place.
paidFrom: You pay only for your server, about $5–20 a month
signupSteps: Rent a small server (VPS)
Run the one-line Coolify installer on it
Open Coolify in your browser and add your apps

name: Stripe
what: Lets your app take card payments safely. You never touch card numbers.
signupSteps: Sign up at stripe.com (test mode works right away)
Copy your test keys from Developers → API keys
Later, finish the business details to take real payments

name: Cloudflare R2
what: Stores files like photos and videos for your app. Downloads are free.
paidFrom: About 1.5¢ per GB after that, no download fees
signupSteps: Sign up at cloudflare.com
Go to R2 and create a bucket
Create an API token for R2

name: Backblaze B2
what: Cheap file storage, great for backups.
signupSteps: Sign up at backblaze.com
Create a bucket
Create an application key

name: Whisper (on your computer)
what: Turns speech into text on your own computer. Free and private.
signupSteps: Your AI helper can add it to your app (via whisper.cpp or faster-whisper)
Or use the Buzz app to try it first

name: SearXNG
what: A free search engine you run yourself. Your app can search the web with it.
signupSteps: Run SearXNG with Docker on your computer or server
Turn on the JSON format in its settings
Your app searches through http://localhost:8080

name: Brave Search API
what: Web search results for your app from an independent search engine.
freeTier: $5 of free credit each month (about 1,000 searches)
signupSteps: Sign up for the Brave Search API
Pick a plan (credit card needed)
Create an API key

name: OpenStreetMap + MapLibre
what: Free world maps for your app, made by volunteers.
paidFrom: Free (heavy use should use a map host)
signupSteps: Nothing to sign up for to start: your AI helper adds MapLibre to the app
For lots of visitors, use a map host with a free plan
note: Show "© OpenStreetMap contributors" on the map.

name: Unsplash API
what: Free, beautiful photos your app can show.
freeTier: 50 requests an hour to start, 5,000 an hour after approval
signupSteps: Sign up at unsplash.com/developers
Create a new app
Copy the Access Key
note: Give credit to the photographer, as Unsplash asks.

name: Jitsi Meet
what: Free video calls you can put inside your app.
signupSteps: Nothing to sign up for to try it: your AI helper can embed a meet.jit.si room
For your own private server, self-host Jitsi

name: LiveKit
what: Video, voice and live audio for apps. Open source, with a free cloud plan.
freeTier: 5,000 minutes a month on the free cloud plan
signupSteps: Sign up at cloud.livekit.io
Create a project
Copy the URL, API key and secret

name: Phaser
what: A free tool for making 2D games that run in a web browser. Share your game with just a link.
signupSteps: Nothing to sign up for.
Your AI helper installs it into your project for you.
note: Phaser 4 came out in April 2026. MIT license.

name: Godot
what: A free game maker for 2D and 3D games. Make games for Windows, Mac, Linux, phones and the web.
freeTier: Free forever, for anything. No fees on sales.
signupSteps: Download Godot from godotengine.org. No account needed.
Unzip it and open it. Your AI helper writes the game files.
note: MIT license. Version 4.7 is the current stable one.

name: Kenney game assets
what: Thousands of free game pictures, sounds and fonts. You can use them for anything, even games you sell.
freeTier: Free (CC0). Giving credit is nice but not needed.
signupSteps: Go to kenney.nl/assets.
Pick a pack and click Download. No account needed.
Unzip it into your game's folder and tell your AI helper.

name: OpenGameArt
what: A big library of free game art and music made by the community. Each file has its own license.
freeTier: Free. Check each file's license (CC0, CC BY, GPL and more).
signupSteps: Search opengameart.org for what you need.
Check the license on the file's page.
Write the author and license in your CREDITS.md.

name: Freesound
what: Free sound effects made by people all over the world: jumps, coins, doors, rain.
freeTier: Free with an account. Each sound is CC0, CC BY, or CC BY-NC (no selling).
signupSteps: Make a free account at freesound.org.
Search for a sound and check its license.
Download it and add it to your CREDITS.md.

name: itch.io
what: A free place to share your game. People can play it in their browser or download it.
freeTier: Free to upload. You choose how much itch.io gets if you sell (10% by default, 0% is allowed).
signupSteps: Make a free account at itch.io.
Click "Upload new project".
For a browser game, upload a ZIP with index.html and tick "played in the browser".

name: GitHub Pages
what: Puts a website or browser game online for free, straight from your code on GitHub.
freeTier: Free for public projects. Up to 1 GB, not for selling things.
signupSteps: Put your game's code on GitHub (your AI helper can walk you through it).
In the project, open Settings → Pages.
Pick your main branch and click Save. Your game gets its own link.
